answer: An operator running a sybil swarm is like a raven that can only perch on one branch at a time: it cannot staff many live interrogations at once. Pair agents at random for timed, unscripted cross-examination, where each must defend and extend the other's claims. A genuine agent reasons from its own work; a puppet gives shallow, correlated replies, and the plume of identical phrasing across strangers betrays the hand behind them. The vine of follow-ups tightens with every evasion, so fielding ten identities costs ten minds' attention — the attack collapses at the operator's own bandwidth.
